2027-03-10.title: Wednesday of the fifth week of the Great Fast
readings: The children of Nahor; Rebekah's family
Elders who rule well are worthy of double honour
2027-03-10.verse: I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat;
theo: After the drama of Moriah, Genesis seems to change the subject: “Now after these things it was told Abraham, ‘Milcah also has borne children, to your brother Nahor.’” A list of names follows, and among them one short sentence: “Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.” It is easy to skip, but it is the hinge of the next chapter. While Abraham was climbing the mountain with Isaac, God was already preparing, far away in Haran, the girl who would one day be Isaac's wife and the mother of Jacob. God's promises do not move forward only through visions and angels; they move through births, families and ordinary news. St Paul says that “when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman”; the long genealogies of the Bible are the patient road by which that fullness came. No family is too ordinary to be part of God's plan.

The Gospel shows the same God, now in the flesh, caring for ordinary needs. “I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away hungry, for they might faint on the way.” The disciples see only the desert: “Where are we to get enough bread in the desert to feed so great a crowd?” Jesus asks what they have, “Seven, and a few small fish,” and then does what he will do at the Last Supper: “he took the seven loaves and the fish; and after giving thanks he broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.” Many Fathers noted that this second feeding took place among people from the Gentile side of the lake, a sign that the Bread of Life is for all nations. Notice the order: Christ gives to the disciples, and the disciples give to the people. That is the ministry of the priest at the Holy Qurbono, and it is why the Letter to Timothy says: “Let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching.” The same passage asks for justice (“Never accept any accusation against an elder except on the evidence of two or three witnesses”) and for great care in choosing them: “Do not ordain anyone hastily.” St Ignatius of Antioch urged the faithful to respect their presbyters as the council of God and the college of the apostles (in substance). To honour our priests is to honour the Lord who feeds us through their hands; to pray for them is to share in their work.
outline: Ask: who fed you with the word of God when you were young?
Point 1 · Bethuel became the father of Rebekah
Priests who labour in preaching and teaching.
live: Thank a priest of your parish this week in person or with a short note, and pray for him by name each day.
Give from your own food this week to someone who has little, as the disciples gave the seven loaves.
2027-03-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you had compassion on the hungry crowd and fed them with seven loaves, giving thanks, breaking and giving through your disciples. Bless the priests who give us your word and your Body and Blood; keep them holy, guard them from injustice, and send good workers into your harvest. As you prepared Rebekah's family long before she was needed, prepare our families for your plan. Amen.
altar: At the altar Christ still takes the bread, gives thanks, breaks it and gives it through the hands of his priests, so that no one need faint on the way.

quick: News came to Abraham of his brother Nahor's family; Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.
Elders who rule well, especially in preaching and teaching, are worthy of double honour; choose them with care.
Jesus had compassion on the crowd and fed four thousand with seven loaves.
2027-03-10.action: Thank a priest and pray for him by name.
2027-03-10.question: Do I honour and pray for those who feed me with God's word?

family.explain: Jesus saw that the people were hungry and felt sorry for them. The disciples had only seven loaves and a few fish, but Jesus thanked God, broke the bread and gave it to the disciples to share. Everyone ate and there were seven baskets left over! Today Jesus still gives us the Bread of Life through our priests at the Holy Qurbono.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for all priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone who is hungry?”

illus: In a high-range parish in Idukki, an old priest kept a jar of rice by the sacristy door. Anyone could take a measure, no questions asked, and anyone could add one. After his funeral the parishioners found a school notebook in his room. On every page he had written the names of families he had brought Holy Communion to in their homes, with small notes: knee pain, son abroad, waiting for rain. On the last page was a line he must have written for himself: they gave me the bread; I only carried it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have compassion on all who are hungry. Feed us with your word and your Body. Amen.
share: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah (Genesis 22:23). Where has God been quietly preparing something good in my family?
Let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor (1 Timothy 5:17). How do I honour and support my priests?
I have compassion for the crowd (Matthew 15:32). Whose hunger have I noticed this week?
interc: For our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops and all priests.
For priests who are tired, sick or falsely accused.
For young men discerning a call to the priesthood.
For the hungry in our town and in the world.
For our families, that we may see God's hand in ordinary days.
pm.close: Father, your Son had compassion on the crowd and fed them in the desert. Bless the priests who break the bread of life for us, and make us generous in sharing our bread with others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, after Moriah Genesis gives us a list of names, and in it one small sentence: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah (Genesis 22:23). While Abraham was on the mountain, God was already preparing Isaac's future wife. God works through ordinary families.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat (Matthew 15:32). The disciples have only seven loaves and a few small fish.

Jesus took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds (Matthew 15:36). This is what happens at every Holy Qurbono: Christ gives, and the priest hands on what he has received.

So Paul writes: let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching (1 Timothy 5:17). Let us thank God for our priests, pray for them, and share our bread with the hungry. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus saw that the people were hungry and he felt sorry for them. With only seven loaves he fed thousands of people! At church the priest gives us Jesus, the Bread of Life. Tonight, say a prayer for your parish priest, and share something you like with someone else.

intro: Theme: “I have compassion for the crowd.”
God's quiet preparation in ordinary families, the honour due to those who feed us, and the Lord who takes, gives thanks, breaks and gives.

concl: God prepares his future through ordinary families and feeds his people through his priests.
Christ still has compassion on the hungry crowd and gives himself as the Bread of Life.
